text: Let $f(x)=3\sqrt{x-2}+\sqrt{4-x}$ be a real valued function. If $α$ and $β$ are respectively the minimum and the maximum values of $f$, then $α^{2}+2β^{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f$ is defined when $x-2\geq 0$ and $4-x\geq 0$, i.e. on $[2,4]$. For $2<x<4$,

$f^{'}(x)=\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt{x-2}}-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{4-x}}$

$f^{'}(x)=0\Rightarrow 3\sqrt{4-x}=\sqrt{x-2}\Rightarrow 9(4-x)=x-2\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{19}{5}$

As $x$ increases, $\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt{x-2}}$ decreases and $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{4-x}}$ increases, so $f^{'}$ is decreasing: $f^{'}>0$ on $\left (2,\dfrac{19}{5}\right )$ and $f^{'}<0$ on $\left (\dfrac{19}{5},4\right )$.

So the maximum is at $x=\dfrac{19}{5}$:

$β=3\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{5}}+\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{5}}=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{5}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}=2\sqrt{5}$

The minimum is at an end point: $f(2)=\sqrt{2}$ and $f(4)=3\sqrt{2}$, so $α=\sqrt{2}$.

$α^{2}+2β^{2}=2+2(20)=42$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Given that the inverse trigonometric function assumes principal values only. Let $x,y$ be any two real numbers in $[-1,1]$ such that $\cos ^{-1}x-\sin ^{-1}y=α,\frac{-π}{2}\leq α\leq π$.
Then, the minimum value of $x^{2}+y^{2}+2xy\sin α$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\sin ^{-1}y=\dfrac{π}{2}-\cos ^{-1}y$, the condition becomes $\cos ^{-1}x+\cos ^{-1}y=\dfrac{π}{2}+α$.

Taking the cosine of both sides, with $\sin (\cos ^{-1}x)=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$ and $\sin (\cos ^{-1}y)=\sqrt{1-y^{2}}$:

$xy-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}=\cos \left (\frac{π}{2}+α\right )=-\sin α\Rightarrow xy+\sin α=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}$

Squaring:

$x^{2}y^{2}+2xy\sin α+\sin ^{2}α=1-x^{2}-y^{2}+x^{2}y^{2}\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+2xy\sin α=1-\sin ^{2}α=\cos ^{2}α$

So the expression always equals $\cos ^{2}α\geq 0$; a negative value such as $-1$ is impossible.

The value 0 is attained: $x=y=0$ gives $α=\cos ^{-1}0-\sin ^{-1}0=\dfrac{π}{2}$, which lies in $\left [-\dfrac{π}{2},π\right ]$, and the expression is then 0. So the minimum value is 0.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: For $λ>0$, let $θ$ be the angle between the vectors $⃗{a}=\hat{i}+λ\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ and $⃗{b}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. If the vectors $⃗{a}+⃗{b}$ and $⃗{a}-⃗{b}$ are mutually perpendicular, then the value of $(14\cos θ)^{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We are given the vectors

$⃗{a}=\hat{i}+λ\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\text{and}⃗{b}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k},$

with $λ>0$, and we are told that the vectors $⃗{a}+⃗{b}$ and $⃗{a}-⃗{b}$ are perpendicular. Our goal is to find $(14\cos θ)^{2}$, where $θ$ is the angle between $⃗{a}$ and $⃗{b}$.

Step 1. Use the Perpendicularity Condition
Two vectors are perpendicular if their dot product is zero. So, we require:

$(⃗{a}+⃗{b})\cdot (⃗{a}-⃗{b})=0.$

First, compute $⃗{a}+⃗{b}$ and $⃗{a}-⃗{b}$:

$⃗{a}+⃗{b}=(\hat{i}+3\hat{i})+(λ\hat{j}-\hat{j})+(-3\hat{k}+2\hat{k})=4\hat{i}+(λ-1)\hat{j}-\hat{k}.$

$⃗{a}-⃗{b}=(\hat{i}-3\hat{i})+(λ\hat{j}+\hat{j})+(-3\hat{k}-2\hat{k})=-2\hat{i}+(λ+1)\hat{j}-5\hat{k}.$

Now, take their dot product:

$(4\hat{i}+(λ-1)\hat{j}-\hat{k})\cdot (-2\hat{i}+(λ+1)\hat{j}-5\hat{k})$

$=4(-2)+(λ-1)(λ+1)+(-1)(-5)=-8+(λ^{2}-1)+5.$

$=λ^{2}-4.$

Setting the dot product to zero:

$λ^{2}-4=0⟹λ^{2}=4.$

Since $λ>0$, we have:

$λ=2.$

Step 2. Find the Angle Between $⃗{a}$ and $⃗{b}$
Now that we know $λ=2$, the vectors become:

$⃗{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k},⃗{b}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}.$

The cosine of the angle $θ$ between $⃗{a}$ and $⃗{b}$ is given by:

$\cos θ=\frac{⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}}{\|⃗{a}\|\|⃗{b}\|}.$

Calculate $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}$:

$⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}=(1)(3)+(2)(-1)+(-3)(2)=3-2-6=-5.$

Calculate the magnitudes:

$\|⃗{a}\|=\sqrt{1^{2}+2^{2}+(-3)^{2}}=\sqrt{1+4+9}=\sqrt{14}.$

$\|⃗{b}\|=\sqrt{3^{2}+(-1)^{2}+2^{2}}=\sqrt{9+1+4}=\sqrt{14}.$

Thus,

$\cos θ=\frac{-5}{\sqrt{14}\cdot \sqrt{14}}=\frac{-5}{14}.$

Step 3. Compute $(14\cos θ)^{2}$
$(14\cos θ)^{2}=\left (14\cdot \frac{-5}{14}\right )^{2}=(-5)^{2}=25.$

Final Answer
The value of $(14\cos θ)^{2}$ is:

$25.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{C}$ be a circle with radius $\sqrt{10}$ units and centre at the origin. Let the line $x+y=2$ intersect the circle $\mathrm{C}$ at the points $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$. Let $\mathrm{MN}$ be a chord of $\mathrm{C}$ of length 2 unit and slope $-1$. Then, a distance (in units) between the chord PQ and the chord $\mathrm{MN}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The circle $C$ is $x^{2}+y^{2}=10$ with centre $O(0,0)$. The chord $MN$ has slope $-1$, so it lies on a line $x+y=λ$.

Half of $MN$ is 1, so the distance of $O$ from $MN$ is $\sqrt{10-1}=3$:

$\frac{|λ|}{\sqrt{2}}=3\Rightarrow λ=\pm 3\sqrt{2}.$

$PQ$ lies on $x+y=2$, and the distance between the parallel lines $x+y=2$ and $x+y=λ$ is $\dfrac{|λ-2|}{\sqrt{2}}$.

For $λ=3\sqrt{2}$ it is $\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}-2}{\sqrt{2}}=3-\sqrt{2}$; for $λ=-3\sqrt{2}$ it is $\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}+2}{\sqrt{2}}=3+\sqrt{2}$, which is not among the options.

So a distance between the chords is $3-\sqrt{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: The area (in sq. units) of the region $S=\{z\in \mathrm{ℂ}:|z-1|\leq 2;(z+\bar{z})+i(z-\bar{z})\leq 2,\mathrm{Im}(z)\geq 0\}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $z=x+iy$: $z+\bar{z}=2x$ and $z-\bar{z}=2iy$, so $i(z-\bar{z})=2i^{2}y=-2y$.

So $S$ is given by $(x-1)^{2}+y^{2}\leq 4$ (the disc of centre $(1,0)$ and radius 2), $2x-2y\leq 2$, that is $y\geq x-1$, and $y\geq 0$.

The line $y=x-1$ passes through the centre $(1,0)$ at $45^{\circ }$ to the $x$-axis. Measuring the angle $θ$ at the centre, $y\geq 0$ keeps $0\leq θ\leq π$ and $y\geq x-1$ keeps $\dfrac{π}{4}\leq θ\leq \dfrac{5π}{4}$, so $S$ is the sector $\dfrac{π}{4}\leq θ\leq π$, of angle $\dfrac{3π}{4}$.

A sector of angle $θ$ in a circle of radius $r$ has area $\dfrac{1}{2}r^{2}θ$:

$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2}\cdot \frac{3π}{4}=\frac{3π}{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Let a relation $\mathrm{R}$ on $\mathrm{ℕ}\times \mathrm{ℕ}$ be defined as: $(x_{1},y_{1})\mathrm{R}(x_{2},y_{2})$ if and only if $x_{1}\leq x_{2}$ or $y_{1}\leq y_{2}$.
Consider the two statements:

(I) $\mathrm{R}$ is reflexive but not symmetric.

(II) $\mathrm{R}$ is transitive

Then which one of the following is true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(x_{1},y_{1})R(x_{2},y_{2})$ holds when at least one of $x_{1}\leq x_{2}$, $y_{1}\leq y_{2}$ is true.

Reflexive: for every $(x,y)$, $x\leq x$, so $(x,y)R(x,y)$.

Not symmetric: $(1,2)R(3,4)$ because $1\leq 3$, but $(3,4)R(1,2)$ fails because $3\leq 1$ and $4\leq 2$ are both false. So statement (I) is correct.

Not transitive: take $(3,9)$, $(4,6)$ and $(2,7)$. $(3,9)R(4,6)$ because $3\leq 4$ (first coordinates), and $(4,6)R(2,7)$ because $6\leq 7$ (second coordinates).

But $(3,9)R(2,7)$ would need $3\leq 2$ or $9\leq 7$, and both are false. The two links use different coordinates, so they force no comparison between $(3,9)$ and $(2,7)$; R is not transitive and statement (II) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lll} \mathrm{adj}(A)=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ (\mathrm{adj}A)^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ (\mathrm{adj}A)^{3}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ (\mathrm{adj}A)^{4}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\ (\mathrm{adj}A)^{r}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & (-2r) \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lll} B=\sum\limits _{r=0}^{10}(\mathrm{adj}A)^{r}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \sum\limits _{r=0}^{10}1 & \sum\limits _{r=0}^{10}(-2r) \\ \sum\limits _{r=0}^{10}(0) & \sum\limits _{r=0}^{10}(1) \end{array}\right ] \\ B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 11 & -110 \\ 0 & 11 \end{array}\right ] \end{array}$

$\text{Sum of elements}=-110+11+11=-88$

text: Let $S=\left \{\sin ^{2}2θ:\left (\sin ^{4}θ+\cos ^{4}θ\right )x^{2}+(\sin 2θ)x+\left (\sin ^{6}θ+\cos ^{6}θ\right )=0 \right.$ has real roots $\}$. If $α$ and $β$ be the smallest and largest elements of the set $S$, respectively, then $3\left ((α-2)^{2}+(β-1)^{2}\right )$ equals $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For real roots

$\begin{array}{l} D\geq 0 \\ \sin ^{2}2θ\geq 4\left (\sin ^{4}θ+\cos ^{4}θ\right )\left (\sin ^{6}θ+\cos ^{6}θ\right ) \end{array}$

Put $\sin ^{2}2θ=t$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow t\geq 4\left (1-\dfrac{t}{2}\right )\left (1-\dfrac{3t}{4}\right ) \\ 2t\geq (2-t)(4-3t) \\ 3t^{2}-12t+8\leq 0 \\ t^{2}-4t+\dfrac{8}{3}\leq 0 \\ (t-2)^{2}+\dfrac{8}{3}-4\leq 0 \\ (t-2)^{2}\leq \dfrac{4}{3} \\ -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\leq t-2\leq \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\ 2-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\leq t\leq 2+\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \because t\in [0,1] \\ \Rightarrow 2-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\leq t\leq 1 \\ α=2-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}},β=1 \\ \Rightarrow 3\left [(α-2)^{2}+(β-1)^{2}\right ]=4 \end{array}$

text:
If $\int \mathrm{cosec}^{5}xdx=α\cot x\mathrm{cosec}x\left (\mathrm{cosec}^{2}x+\frac{3}{2}\right )+β\log _{e}\left |\tan \frac{x}{2}\right |+\mathrm{C}$
where $α,β\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $8(α+β)$ equals $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $I_{n}=\int \mathrm{cosec}^{n}xdx$. Writing $\mathrm{cosec}^{n}x=\mathrm{cosec}^{n-2}x\cdot \mathrm{cosec}^{2}x$ and integrating by parts with $\int \mathrm{cosec}^{2}xdx=-\cot x$:

$I_{n}=-\mathrm{cosec}^{n-2}x\cot x-(n-2)\int \mathrm{cosec}^{n-2}x\cot ^{2}xdx.$

Using $\cot ^{2}x=\mathrm{cosec}^{2}x-1$, the last integral is $I_{n}-I_{n-2}$, so

$(n-1)I_{n}=-\mathrm{cosec}^{n-2}x\cot x+(n-2)I_{n-2}.$

For $n=3$, with $I_{1}=\int \mathrm{cosec}xdx=\log _{e}\left |\tan \dfrac{x}{2}\right |$:

$I_{3}=-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{cosec}x\cot x+\frac{1}{2}\log _{e}\left |\tan \frac{x}{2}\right |.$

For $n=5$:

$I_{5}=-\frac{1}{4}\mathrm{cosec}^{3}x\cot x+\frac{3}{4}I_{3}=-\frac{1}{4}\cot x\mathrm{cosec}x\left (\mathrm{cosec}^{2}x+\frac{3}{2}\right )+\frac{3}{8}\log _{e}\left |\tan \frac{x}{2}\right |+C.$

So $α=-\dfrac{1}{4}$, $β=\dfrac{3}{8}$ and $8(α+β)=8\cdot \dfrac{1}{8}=1$.

Hence, the answer is 1.

text: Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix such that $A\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 3 \\ 7 \end{array}\right ]$ and the determinant of $A$ be 1 . If $A^{-1}=αA+βI$, where $I$ is an identity matrix of order $2\times 2$, then $α+β$ equals $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ b & c \end{array}\right ]$, since $A$ is symmetric. Then

$A\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} a+b \\ b+c \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 3 \\ 7 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow a=3-b,c=7-b.$

$|A|=ac-b^{2}=(3-b)(7-b)-b^{2}=21-10b=1\Rightarrow b=2,$

so $a=1$, $c=5$ and $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 \end{array}\right ]$.

$A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{|A|}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 5 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 5 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{array}\right ].$

Comparing $\left [\begin{array}{ll} 5 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=α\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 \end{array}\right ]+β\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$: the off-diagonal entries give $2α=-2\Rightarrow α=-1$, and the $(1,1)$ entry gives $α+β=5\Rightarrow β=6$ (the $(2,2)$ entry checks: $5α+β=1$).

$α+β=-1+6=5$

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: In a tournament, a team plays 10 matches with probabilities of winning and losing each match as $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$ respectively. Let $x$ be the number of matches that the team wins, and $y$ be the number of matches that team loses. If the probability $\mathrm{P}(|x-y|\leq 2)$ is $p$, then $3^{9}p$ equals $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} x+y=10 \\ A=x-y \\ P(|A|<2)\text{is}P \\ \Rightarrow |A|=2,1,0\Rightarrow A=0,1,-1,2,-2 \\ \Rightarrow x=\dfrac{10+A}{2}\Rightarrow A\in \text{even as}x\in \text{integer} \\ \Rightarrow A=0,-2,2 \\ \Rightarrow P(|A|\leq 2)=P(A=0)+P(A=-2)+P(A=2) \end{array}$

(1) $A=0\Rightarrow x=5=y$

$P(A=0)={}^{10}C_{5}\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )^{5}\left (\frac{2}{3}\right )^{5}$

(2) $A=-2$

$\Rightarrow x=4$ and $y=6$

$P(A=-2)={}^{10}C_{4}\cdot \left (\frac{1}{3}\right )^{4}\left (\frac{2}{3}\right )^{6}$ and

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Similarly,}P(A=2)={}^{10}C_{6}\left (\dfrac{1}{3}\right )^{6}\left (\dfrac{2}{3}\right )^{4} \\ \Rightarrow P(|A|\leq 2)3^{9}=3\left ({}^{10}C_{5}\cdot 2^{5}+{}^{10}C_{4}\cdot 2^{6}+{}^{10}C_{6}\cdot 2^{4}\right ) \\ =8288 \end{array}$

text: Consider the function $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ defined by $f(x)=\frac{2x}{\sqrt{1+9x^{2}}}$. If the composition of $f,(f\circ f\circ f\circ \cdots \circ f)_{10\text{times}}(x)=\frac{2^{10}x}{\sqrt{1+9αx^{2}}}$, then the value of $\sqrt{3α+1}$ is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\frac{2x}{\sqrt{1+9x^{2}}}$

$(f\circ f)(x)=\frac{2f(x)}{\sqrt{1+9(f(x))^{2}}}=\frac{\frac{4x}{\sqrt{1+9x2}}}{\sqrt{1+9\times \frac{4x2}{1+9x2}}}=\frac{4x}{\sqrt{1+45x^{2}}}$

$(f\circ f\circ f)(x)=\frac{4\times \frac{2x}{\sqrt{1+9x2}}}{\sqrt{1+45\times \frac{4x2}{1+9x2}}}=\frac{8x}{\sqrt{1+21\times 9x^{2}}}$

$(f\circ f\circ f\circ f)(x)=\frac{16x}{\sqrt{1+85\times 9x^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow α$ is $10^{\text{th}}$ term of $1,5,21,85,\ldots α$ is $10^{\text{th}}$ term of

$\begin{array}{ll} \qquad \dfrac{\left (2^{1}\right )^{2}-1}{3},\dfrac{\left (2^{2}\right )^{2}-1}{3},\dfrac{\left (2^{3}\right )^{2}-1}{3},\dfrac{\left (2^{4}\right )^{2}-1}{3},\ldots  \\ \Rightarrow \quad  & α=\dfrac{\left (2^{10}\right )^{2}-1}{3} \\ \Rightarrow \quad  & \sqrt{3α+1}=2^{10}=1024 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(x+y+2)^{2}dx=dy,y(0)=-2$. Let the maximum and minimum values of the function $y=y(x)$ in $\left [0,\frac{π}{3}\right ]$ be $α$ and $β$, respectively. If $(3α+π)^{2}+β^{2}=γ+δ\sqrt{3},γ,δ\in \mathrm{ℤ}$, then $γ+δ$ equals $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{dy}{dx}=(x+y+2)^{2} \\ \text{Put}x+y+2=t \\ \Rightarrow 1+\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dt}{dx} \\ \text{Given DE}\Rightarrow \dfrac{dt}{dx}-1=t^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{dt}{1+t^{2}}=dx\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}t=x+c \\ \Rightarrow x+y+2=\tan (x+c) \\ \Rightarrow y(x)=\tan (x+c)-x-2 \\ \because y(0)=-2\Rightarrow -2=\tan c-0-2 \\ \Rightarrow c=0 \\ \Rightarrow y(x)=\tan x-x-2 \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sec ^{2}x-1\geq 0 \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow y(x)$ is increasing if $x\in \left (0,\frac{π}{3}\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow α=y\left (\dfrac{π}{3}\right ),β=y(0) \\ \Rightarrow α=-\dfrac{π}{3}-2+\sqrt{3}\text{and}β=-2 \end{array}$

Now, $(3α+π)^{2}+β^{2}=(3\sqrt{3}-6)^{2}+(-2)^{2}$

$=67-36\sqrt{3}=γ+δ\sqrt{3}$.

$\Rightarrow γ+δ=31$

text: Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be a thrice differentiable function such that $f(0)=0,f(1)=1,f(2)=-1,f(3)=2$ and $f(4)=-2$. Then, the minimum number of zeros of $(3f^{'}f^{''}+ff^{'''})(x)$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(0)=0$, and $f$ takes the values $1,-1,2,-2$ at $x=1,2,3,4$, so by the intermediate value theorem $f$ has zeros $0<a<b<c$ with $a\in (1,2)$, $b\in (2,3)$, $c\in (3,4)$.

By Rolle's theorem, $f^{'}$ has zeros $p\in (0,a)$, $q\in (a,b)$, $r\in (b,c)$.

Let $g=ff^{'}$. Then $g$ vanishes at the 7 distinct points $0<p<a<q<b<r<c$.

$g^{'}=f^{'2}+ff^{''},g^{''}=2f^{'}f^{''}+f^{'}f^{''}+ff^{'''}=3f^{'}f^{''}+ff^{'''}$

By Rolle's theorem, $g^{'}$ has at least 6 distinct zeros, so $g^{''}=3f^{'}f^{''}+ff^{'''}$ has at least 5 distinct zeros.

The bound is attained: the polynomial of degree at most 4 through the five given points has at least 4 zeros and is not zero, so it has degree 4 with exactly the 4 real zeros above; then $g^{''}=\dfrac{1}{2}\left (f^{2}\right )^{'''}$ is a polynomial of degree 5, with at most 5 zeros.

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Consider a line $\mathrm{L}$ passing through the points $\mathrm{P}(1,2,1)$ and $\mathrm{Q}(2,1,-1)$. If the mirror image of the point $\mathrm{A}(2,2,2)$ in the line $\mathrm{L}$ is $(α,β,γ)$, then $α+β+6γ$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} A(2,2,2) \\ PQ:\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y-2}{-1}=\dfrac{z-1}{-2} \end{array}$

General point,

$(k+1,-k+2,-2k+1)$

$\begin{array}{l} OA\leftarrow =(k+1-2)\hat{i}+(-k+2-2)\hat{j}+(-2k+1-2)\hat{k} \\ OA\leftarrow =(k-1)\hat{i}-k\hat{j}+(-2k-1)\hat{k} \\ PQ\leftarrow =1\hat{i}-\hat{j}-2\hat{k} \\ OA\leftarrow \cdot PQ\leftarrow =0 \\ (k-1)+k+2(2k+1)=0 \\ k-1+k+4k+2=0 \\ 6k+1=0 \\ k=\dfrac{-1}{6} \\ 0\left (\dfrac{-1}{6}+1,\dfrac{+1}{6}+2,-2\left (\dfrac{-1}{6}\right )+1\right ) \\ 0\left (\dfrac{5}{6},\dfrac{13}{6},\dfrac{8}{6}\right ) \\ 0\left (\dfrac{5}{6},\dfrac{13}{6},\dfrac{8}{6}\right )=\left (\dfrac{α+2}{2},\dfrac{β+2}{2},\dfrac{γ+2}{2}\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} α+2=\frac{10}{6} & β+2=\frac{26}{6} \\ α=\frac{10}{6}-2 & β=\frac{26-12}{6} \\ α=\frac{-2}{6} & β=\frac{14}{6} \\ α=-\frac{1}{3} & β=\frac{7}{3} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} γ+2=\dfrac{16}{6} \\ γ=\dfrac{16-12}{6} \\ γ=\dfrac{4}{6} \\ \Rightarrow α+β+6γ \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{-1}{3}+\dfrac{7}{3}+6\times \dfrac{4}{6} \\ \Rightarrow 2+4=6 \end{array}$
